title: Simulation of First-Component Equality
statement: Let $m,d$ be natural numbers, let $\Lambda$ be a type of labels, and let $A$ assign an instruction to each label, with initial label $l_0$. Let an oracle assign a Boolean answer to each decider in a set of $d$ deciders and each bit string, and let $x$ be a valid nested pair encoding. Suppose $l,l_1,l_0'\in\Lambda$, $r$ is one of the $m$ registers, and the instruction at $l$ tests whether the binary expansion of register $r$ equals the first component of the inner pair, branching to $l_1$ on equality and to $l_0'$ otherwise. For any register valuation $v$, output word, and integer bound $W$ such that the length of the binary expansion of $v(r)$ is at most $W$, the compiled program simulates this instruction from the configuration with input $x$, label $l$, valuation $v$, and the given output word to the configuration with the same input, valuation, and output, and with label $l_1$ exactly when the binary expansion of $v(r)$ equals the first inner component extracted from $x$, and label $l_0'$ otherwise. At every intermediate configuration before the endpoint, no oracle call is pending and every work-tape head position lies between $-1$ and $W$, inclusive.
hypotheses_covered: Instruction map A and initial label l₀
Oracle assigning Boolean answers by decider and bit string
Register r among the m registers
Length of Nat.bits(v(r)) is at most W
